pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Under the Surface is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk, and swim. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

Fall in the water on purpose and watch which way it takes Kit. Water is friendly in this game, and nothing in it can hurt you.

pages.head: Level 1: The Creek
pages.html:
Level 1: The Creek

THIS WATER PULLS LEFT. FALL IN AND IT CARRIES YOU BACK is the first sign. Step into the creek and hold Right: the water wins, and carries Kit back to the bank he came from. NOTHING HERE HURTS. HOP THE STONES TO CROSS is the second. Jump from stone to stone, take the coins and walk into the door at the right.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Water is a gravity setting. Open sw.bbl in the block editor and look at creek and creekTop. Each has Gravity set to left and down. A block with no pull at all would be plain air, and the hero is pulled by the block he is standing in.
  • The pull is the whole current. Every tick the block adds a little to Kit's speed in each direction it names, up to a limit, so walking against the creek cannot beat it. The picture of chevrons is only there to show you the way.
  • Nothing here hurts. A block can take hit points when touched, but these have none. The creek is two blocks deep, with the ground below it, so Kit lands on the bottom and is carried along it.
  • The stepping stones are a block that is solid on top only, so you can jump up through them and land on them, with the creek's pull set on them too. Open one.map to see where each is placed.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the right to the next level in sw.gam.

pages.head: Level 2: The Float
pages.html:
Level 2: The Float

THIS WATER PULLS UP, SO KIT FLOATS comes first. Walk off the bank into the pool: Kit does not sink but rises to the top and stays there. THE TOP ROW HAS NO PULL. KIT SETTLES THERE is on the far bank. Swim across with the arrow keys, take the coins that hang just over the water and walk into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Water that pulls up. Open sw.bbl and look at the block deep: its Gravity is up. Where ordinary air pulls down, this pulls the other way, so anything in it rises.
  • The top row has no pull. The block deepTop has Gravity set to nothing at all. Upward speed fades there instead of building, so Kit settles at the surface instead of shooting out of the pool. It is a lighter blue with foam, so you can see which row it is.
  • Swimming is just walking. The walking sequence works in the water the same as on land, so the arrow keys carry Kit across. A bank at each end is ordinary ground.
  • The pool is a hole in the ground. Open two.map: a row of deepTop at the level of the ground, and four rows of deep under it, with dirt below.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. A scene link joins the door at the right to the next level in sw.gam.

pages.head: Level 3: The Lift
pages.html:
Level 3: The Lift

THIS WATER PULLS UP AND LEFT. STEP IN is the sign on the low floor. Walk left into the tall pool and let it take you: Kit rises in a curve and pops up at the top beside the cliff. THE TOP ROW HAS NO PULL, SO WALK OUT HERE is on the ledge. Take the coins and walk left into the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • Two pulls at once. Open sw.bbl and look at lift: its Gravity has up and left both on. The two add together, so Kit curves up and to the left, the way the arrows in the water point.
  • The same surface trick. liftTop has no pull, so Kit settles at the top row and can walk out onto the ledge, which is at the same height.
  • The level goes the other way. The door is on the left, because the lift pulls left. A level does not have to run left to right.
  • No coins in the water. A coin that is touched becomes ordinary air, and air pulls down. Coins in the pool would leave holes that pull, so they are placed in the air above it.
  • The signs and the exit. The signs are ordinary blocks with words in their pictures. The last door links to the The End scene in sw.gam.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine's limits, so you can plan around them.

  • It cannot make a real current or buoyancy. A pull is on or off. It speeds Kit up a step every tick up to a top speed, so water cannot be gentle, and he cannot be held at a depth. He floats up and settles only because a row with no pull is above it.
  • It cannot slow him down. A block cannot add drag, so there is no thick water or slow wading. Walking against a strong pull simply loses.
  • It cannot tell water from air. Water is only a block with a gravity setting. There is no swimming sequence, no breath to run out and no splash when he goes in, unless you draw them in the blocks and the hero's frames.
  • It cannot pull things that are not the hero. The gravity setting moves the hero. Monsters have their own movement, so they do not float or drift in a creek.
  • It cannot pull from where he is not. The pull comes from the block Kit is mostly in, so a pool is a place made of blocks, and its edges are where the blocks end.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Set the creek's gravity to right and down, and watch it carry Kit across to the far bank.
  • Turn off the left on the lift, so it only pulls up.
  • Give the top row of the deep pool the same pull as the rest, and watch him bob.
  • Draw a new picture for a water block, with ripples or fish.
  • Move the stepping stones closer together or further apart.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
